title: Hello, Python!
objectives: Learn how to display text using the print() function
Understand string literals and basic syntax rules

body.content: Welcome to Python! In programming, the very first thing most learners do is make the computer display a message on the screen. In Python, we do this with the `print()` function.

body.caption: Running this code outputs: Hello, PyQuest!

body.title: Quotation Marks Matter
body.text: Text in Python must be enclosed in single quotes ('...') or double quotes ("..."). These are called strings.

body.question: Which of the following correctly prints the word 'Welcome' to the terminal?
body.explanation: Python uses the built-in print() function followed by parentheses and quoted text.

exercise.instructions: Write code to print the exact message `Hello, World!` to standard output.

visibleTests.feedbackOnFail: Expected 'Hello, World!' but received different output. Check punctuation and spelling.

hints: Put the text inside double quotes inside parentheses: print("Hello, World!")
